text:
## Japanese

> ご返信が遅くなりましたこと、心よりお詫び申し上げます。
> 本件につきまして確認いたしましたところ、本日中に交換品を発送させていただきます。

**Romanised:**
*Go-henshin ga osoku narimashita koto, kokoro yori owabi mōshiagemasu.
Honken ni tsukimashite kakunin itashimashita tokoro, honjitsu-chū ni kōkanhin o hassō sasete itadakimasu.*

### Register notes
- **心よりお詫び申し上げます** (*kokoro yori owabi mōshiagemasu*): a standard, very formal apology using humble language (*kenjōgo*). It is more formal than 申し訳ございません (*mōshiwake gozaimasen*).
- **ご返信** (*go-henshin*): the honorific prefix *go-* is conventionally attached to one's own reply when it is directed to the customer.
- **本件につきまして** (*honken ni tsukimashite*): a formal version of "regarding this matter."
- **確認いたしましたところ** (*kakunin itashimashita tokoro*): humble form of "checked," with *tokoro* meaning "upon doing so / as a result."
- **本日中に** (*honjitsu-chū ni*): formal "within today." 本日 is used instead of the casual 今日.
- **発送させていただきます** (*hassō sasete itadakimasu*): a deferential way of saying "we will send," literally "we will humbly be permitted to send."

## Back-translation (literal)

> "We offer our heartfelt apologies for the fact that our reply became late.
> Regarding this matter, upon having (humbly) checked, we will humbly be permitted to dispatch the replacement item within today."

**Natural English rendering:**
"Please accept our sincere apologies for the delay in replying. Having looked into the matter, we will dispatch a replacement to you today."

The meaning is preserved. The Japanese adds layers of humility, such as "humbly be permitted to," that English expresses only through tone and word choice like "sincerely."
